source.publication: 2025 IT-511 Individual Income Tax Booklet (Georgia DOR), with Form 500 and Schedule 1 bound in (PDF pages 41-49)
source.section: Form 500 lines 8-16 (booklet PDF pp.16-17: Line 8 federal AGI, Line 10 Georgia AGI, Line 11 standard deduction, Lines 13-15c, Line 16 'Multiply the amount on Line 15c by 5.19%. Round to nearest dollar.'); Form 500 Schedule 1 page 1 lines 1-14 (PDF p.47); rate cite PDF p.9 What's New; standard deduction cite PDF p.16 Line 11

worked: Federal AGI = wages 40,000.00 = 40,000.00. Federal taxable income = 40,000.00 - (standard deduction 23,625.00) = 16,375.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; federal figures are given, not tested; Georgia starts from federal AGI). Age 40: no retirement exclusion. Georgia's head of household standard deduction is 12,000, the same as single (PDF p.16 Line 11). No dependents are entered (the dependent exemption is not modelled and checks carry no dependents). Schedule 1 additions lines 1-5 none, line 6 = 0.00. Schedule 1 line 13 total subtractions = none = 0.00; line 14 net adjustments = 0.00. Form 500 line 8 federal AGI 40,000.00; line 9 = 0.00; line 10 Georgia AGI = 40,000.00 - 0.00 = 40,000.00. Line 11 standard deduction (head of household) 12,000.00 (the filer takes the federal standard deduction, so must take Georgia's); line 13 = 40,000.00 - 12,000.00 = 28,000.00; line 14 dependent exemption 0 dependents = 0.00; line 15a = 28,000.00; line 15b NOL 0.00; line 15c = 28,000.00. Line 16 tax = 5.19% x 28,000.00 = 1,453.2000 = 1,453.20; the form rounds to the nearest dollar and gives 1,453; expected uses the unrounded formula to the cent. Line 17 Low Income Credit: federal AGI is not under 20,000, so none; no other credits; credits 0.00; state income tax = 1,453.20.
